evals.prompt: I've got a local checkout of gpui-go at ~/src/gpui-go (the Go port of Zed's GPUI). Make me a new Go module in ./todo-app with a small desktop todo list: 1000 items, rendered with a uniform list so it stays fast, up/down arrow keys move the selection (the list should scroll to keep it visible), space toggles done (strike-through), and clicking a row selects it. Add tests for the keyboard behaviour and the click.
evals.expected_output: A Go module whose go.mod requires github.com/megascan/gpui-go v0.0.0 with a replace to the checkout. main.go defines three registered actions, a TodoList view with focus handle, Drop, uniform list in a bounded-height flex column, KeyContext + TrackFocus + OnAction wiring, BindKeys with a matching context, DefaultWindowOptions and initial focus. main_test.go uses gpui.RunTest with AddWindowView, SimulateKeystrokes and DebugBounds + SimulateClick. go vet and go test pass.
expectations: go.mod requires github.com/megascan/gpui-go and has a replace directive pointing at the local checkout
The window is opened from gpui.DefaultWindowOptions() (not a bare gpui.WindowOptions{} literal)
Rows are rendered with gpui.NewUniformList, and the list has a bounded height (Flex1/HFull/H inside a sized parent)
Each action type implements Name, BoxedClone and PartialEq and is registered with gpui.RegisterAction in init (or generated by actiongen)
The root element has KeyContext matching the context passed to gpui.NewKeyBinding, plus TrackFocus with the view's focus handle and OnAction handlers
The focus handle is released in a Drop(cx *gpui.App) method and the initial focus handle obtained in OpenWindow is released after focusing
Selection changes call ScrollToItem on a UniformListScrollHandle attached with TrackUniformListScroll
The row callback does not use cx.Processor (avoids the strong-handle leak); it reads a render-time snapshot or a WeakEntity
Row click handlers are attached after .ID(...) on each row
Tests use gpui.RunTest and AddWindowView, release the view, and simulate keystrokes and a click located via DebugSelector/DebugBounds
go vet ./... and go test ./... both succeed with cgo enabled (no leaked-handle panic)

evals.expected_output: A Go Stopwatch struct with a *gpui.Task field and []gpui.Subscription field, a constructor that spawns via cx.Spawn with a WeakEntity, Await on a BackgroundExecutor timer, stops the loop on the WeakEntity.Update error, a Drop that cancels the task and unsubscribes, a Render using NewDiv/Gap2/P(gpui.Px(8))/ID/CursorPointer/Hover with BindStyled/OnClick(cx.Listener(...)), and a RunTest test that advances the fake clock with cx.Executor().AdvanceClock.
expectations: The Rust _ticker task becomes a stored *gpui.Task field that is Cancel()ed in Drop(cx *gpui.App)
The Rust _subs subscriptions are stored and Unsubscribe()d in Drop (not left to the GC)
The loop awaits cx.BackgroundExecutor().Timer(time.Second).Await(cx) and exits when WeakEntity.Update returns an error
Hover is implemented with a bound gpui.Styled[*gpui.StyleRefinement] (BindStyled), not a nonexistent fluent method on *StyleRefinement
OnClick is called after .ID("toggle") and uses cx.Listener with *gpui.ClickEvent
Lengths are typed (gpui.Px(8)), and strings use ChildText or SharedString Child
The test uses gpui.RunTest and cx.Executor().AdvanceClock(...) followed by RunUntilParked, not time.Sleep
The test releases every entity it creates, and go test passes under the default strict leak detection
The answer notes at least one Go deviation it applied (explicit Release/Cancel/Unsubscribe for Rust drops, R-suffix methods, or unchecked EventEmitter)

evals.prompt: In my gpui-go app (package main, view type `Settings` in settings.go) there's a 'Reset' button: `gpui.NewDiv().ID("reset").OnClick(cx.Listener(func(this *Settings, _ *gpui.ClickEvent, _ *gpui.Window, cx *gpui.Context[Settings]) { this.volume = 50; cx.Notify() })).ChildText("Reset")`. Write a test that actually clicks the button through the window (not by calling the method) and checks volume goes back to 50 after I set it to 10.
evals.expected_output: A settings_test.go that uses gpui.RunTest, opens the view with tc.Cx().AddWindowView, releases it, adds DebugSelector to the button (or explains it must be added), resizes/parks, finds bounds with DebugBounds, clicks the centre with SimulateClick, runs until parked and reads the volume via the VisualTestContext.
expectations: The test is wrapped in gpui.RunTest(t, func(tc *gpui.TestRun) {...})
The window and view come from tc.Cx().AddWindowView, and the returned view is released (defer view.Release())
The button gets a DebugSelector (code change shown) and the test locates it with cx.DebugBounds
The click is performed with cx.SimulateClick(bounds.Center(), gpui.Modifiers{}) (optionally preceded by SimulateMouseMove)
cx.RunUntilParked() is called after the click before asserting
State is set to 10 via an entity update and read back via ReadWith/UpdateR, not by mutating fields outside an update
The answer mentions that DebugSelector is a no-op under -tags gpui_release

evals.expected_output: Explains that a bare WindowOptions literal leaves Show false (macOS hides it, Linux ignores it) and fixes it with DefaultWindowOptions; explains that Child(r.sidebar) moves the handle each frame (use Clone), that the sidebar handle must be released in Root.Drop, and that the Observe subscription must be stored and Unsubscribed (or Detached); provides corrected code and suggests LEAK_BACKTRACE=1.
expectations: Identifies the gpui.WindowOptions{} literal leaving Show=false as the macOS cause and replaces it with gpui.DefaultWindowOptions() plus field assignment
Notes that Linux ignores Show, which is why it works there
Identifies that Child(r.sidebar) consumes the handle and changes it to Child(r.sidebar.Clone())
Adds a Drop(cx *gpui.App) on Root that releases the sidebar entity
Stores the Observe subscription and Unsubscribes it in Drop (or explicitly Detaches it)
Handles the error returned by cx.OpenWindow instead of discarding it
Mentions LEAK_BACKTRACE=1 for finding allocation sites
